item: Row 382 (R800): the custody chain verify says whether this installation's custody key signed the chain
summary: GET /api/custody/{item}/verify checked each entry against the key it carries and anchored the lineage on the last entry's own key, so a verified chain said nothing about who signed it. A verified reply now carries signed_by and signer_key: the anchor key (the last entry's Ed25519 key) compared with this installation's custody Ed25519 key, read as POST /verify reads it (no key or folder created), through R801's one comparison point evidence.is_this_installations_key asked about keys/custody_ed25519.pem, so a restore marker beside that key counts. States: this-installation, another-installation, not-compared (no custody key here or it cannot be read); a chain that does not verify names no signer. The custody view shows R800's existing labels x12 (Signed by this installation / another installation / Signed by key, each with the key's first 16 hex characters); no new strings; what a chain is accepted as is unchanged. Known gap, ruled as row 393 (R816): a restore places custody and annotations keys with no R801 marker, so until that lands a custody key restored from another computer reads as this installation's here and in POST /verify.
